description: Capture and resolve the nine Astra xhigh feature reviews of release/3.0 at fb5b59bd. Findings cover conformance, security boundaries, simplification, maintainability, authoring, and independent package quality. Full review reports are preserved in comments; child issues combine duplicate findings. Existing GitHub #79 Cowlib and #81 legacy notification follow-ups remain separate, as does the Jido Git-to-Hex release prerequisite. Do not modify jido_mcp or publish packages. Review probes used current source with isolated processes; shared local build artifacts were stale v2, so final fixes require fresh matching v3 verification. Sequence: authorization and redaction defects first, then runtime/contract correctness, then authoring/docs and design improvements. No implementation is part of this intake.

Full independent review: Jido Connect v3 review: Connector DSL
Source task: 01a09c57-1cfa-7d40-bb71-a5688aa49672

Reviewed `release/3.0` at `fb5b59bda429b7545f82072dabe10f8b299432dc`. The checkout remained clean.

The confirmed defects are below, in priority order. Most require an invalid or conflicting declaration; I did not establish failures in existing provider actions.

1. **P2 — Legacy write declarations can omit confirmation.**  
   [spec/validator.ex:57](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect/lib/jido_connect/contracts/spec/validator.ex:57) checks `mutation?` but does not check write risk. A declaration with only `risk :external_write` produces `mutation?: false` and `confirmation: :none`. The current authorization function then returns `:ok` for an AI actor with `direct_mutation_mode: :deny`.  
   **Correction:** Validate risk, mutation, and confirmation together for both supported declaration forms.

2. **P2 — An auth default can expand the allowed profile list.**  
   [spec_builder.ex:288](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect/lib/jido_connect/dsl/spec_builder.ex:288) adds the default to the list before validation. With both profiles defined, `auth [:tenant], default: :other` produces `auth_profiles: [:other, :tenant]`. Runtime authorization uses this expanded list. The later membership check cannot detect the invalid declaration.  
   **Correction:** Require an explicit default to be a member of the declared list before normalization.

3. **P2 — Duplicate fields replace earlier constraints without an error.**  
   [schema.ex:12](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect/lib/jido_connect/support/schema.ex:12) uses `Map.new/1`. The Spark field entity has no uniqueness identifier. Declaring required string `:id`, followed by optional integer `:id`, accepts both `%{}` and `%{id: 3}`. The stored field list still contains both declarations. This also affects named schemas.  
   **Correction:** Reject duplicate field names before schema construction. Apply the same check to direct contract construction.

4. **P2 — Enum members and defaults can bypass the declared field type.**  
   [schema.ex:44](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect/lib/jido_connect/support/schema.ex:44) replaces the base type with `Zoi.enum/1`. An integer field with `enum: ["wrong"]` accepts `"wrong"` and exports a string schema. At [schema.ex:79](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect/lib/jido_connect/support/schema.ex:79), an integer field with `default: "wrong"` returns that string when input omits the field.  
   **Correction:** Validate enum members and defaults against the base type and its constraints before applying enum or default behavior.

5. **P2 — Different operation names can produce the same generated module.**  
   [projection_builder.ex:11](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect/lib/jido_connect/jido/projection_builder.ex:11) maps both `:foo_bar` and `:foo__bar` to `Actions.FooBar`. The projection check confirmed two different operation IDs with that same module. Spark checks the original names, so it does not detect this collision. The generator emits two definitions for one module. Sensors use the same naming method.  
   **Correction:** Check generated module names for duplicates before generating module code.

6. **P2 — Webhook validation accepts `kind: :none` when the map has another key.**  
   [operation_rules.ex:198](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect/lib/jido_connect/dsl/operation_rules.ex:198) compares complete maps. Thus, `verification %{kind: :none, header: "x-signature"}` passes. [spec/validator.ex:73](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect/lib/jido_connect/contracts/spec/validator.ex:73) repeats this check. This breaks the declaration requirement; it does not establish a bypass in provider webhook processing.  
   **Correction:** Check the `kind` value independently of other map keys. Reject a missing kind and `:none`.

7. **P2 — Generated provider packages do not register for catalog discovery.**  
   [provider_scaffold.ex:74](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect/lib/jido_connect/dev/provider_scaffold.ex:74) generates application settings with only `extra_applications`. [discovery.ex:19](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect/lib/jido_connect/catalog/discovery.ex:19) finds installed providers through `:jido_connect_providers`. Therefore, a generated package remains absent from normal discovery unless the host adds separate configuration. The scaffold test checks file contents but does not check registration.  
   **Correction:** Generate `env: [jido_connect_providers: [ProviderModule]]` in the package application settings.

8. **P3 — Mixed effect settings discard provider idempotency.**  
   [operation_rules.ex:149](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect/lib/jido_connect/dsl/operation_rules.ex:149) does not include top-level `provider_idempotency?` in its mixed-form check. An action with `effect :external_write, confirmation: :required_for_ai` and top-level `provider_idempotency? true` compiles with that value set to `false`.  
   **Correction:** Reject this combination and direct the author to put the option inside `effect`.

Two design improvements have concrete maintenance value:

- **P3 — Reduce repeated validation.** [build_spec.ex:14](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect/lib/jido_connect/dsl/transformers/build_spec.ex:14) runs operation rules before construction. The verifier runs them again, and `Spec.Validator` repeats several rules. The confirmation and webhook defects show why these paths need one shared rule definition.
- **P3 — Preserve field guidance in exported schemas.** [schema.ex:16](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect/lib/jido_connect/support/schema.ex:16) omits field descriptions and examples. They remain in `Field` records but disappear from generated JSON schemas. Copy this guidance into schema metadata so tool consumers can use it.

The focused checks also found two **upstream Zoi 0.18.7 limits**. Its enum parser ignores attached minimum constraints, while its JSON output includes them. Its enum JSON encoder always emits `"type": "string"`, including for `[1, 2]`. See [enum.ex:50](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/deps/zoi/lib/zoi/types/enum.ex:50) and [enum.ex:109](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/deps/zoi/lib/zoi/types/enum.ex:109). These need an upstream correction or a narrow Connect guard.

Cleanup order: fix effect and auth validation; fix field validation and name collisions; fix webhook checks and scaffold registration; then consolidate validation and preserve field guidance.

Coverage included all core DSL entities, sections, rule checks, spec construction, schema conversion, related contracts, generated projections, MCP declarations, authoring guides, scaffold code, and relevant tests and callers. `bw prime` and `git diff --check` completed.

Verification used current source in temporary processes with matching Spark and Zoi versions. The [Spark reproduction](/var/folders/8l/nyn2qp4d441b1zrgypxgry7m0000gn/T/jido-connect-dsl-review-pneymhj8/spark_review.exs) stops after spec construction. Saved build files contained Jido v2, so I did not use them to verify v3 adapters or rerun the full suite. No source, dependencies, branch state, issues, or packages were changed.

Full independent review: Jido Connect v3 review: Jido adapters
Source task: 01a09c57-1efd-7e03-b335-4810b34600d9

Reviewed `release/3.0` at `fb5b59bda429b7545f82072dabe10f8b299432dc`. The checkout is clean and unchanged.

**Confirmed defects**

1. **P1 — Catalog filters can replace the host policy.**  
   [input.ex:116](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect/lib/jido_connect/catalog/input.ex:116) accepts every atom key. [input.ex:71](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect/lib/jido_connect/catalog/input.ex:71) then merges filters after host runtime options.

   An action input with `filters: %{policy: nil}` removes a supplied deny policy. I reproduced this option replacement. `Catalog.call_tool/3` passes these options to Connect, where an absent policy permits operations with `host_policy_required?: false`. Existing catalog tests cover invalid filter shapes, but not runtime keys inside filters.

   **Smallest correction:** Permit only declared filter keys for both atom and string input. Reject runtime keys before the merge.

2. **P2 — Webhook sensor errors can expose secrets.**  
   [sensor_runtime.ex:63](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect/jido/sensor_runtime.ex:63) converts the complete event to a string with `inspect/1`.

   If a caller passes an event containing `access_token`, the returned error includes its value. Later error serialization cannot redact it: the sanitizer only truncates strings. An isolated check retained `REVIEW_SENTINEL` in this error shape; structured input correctly redacted it. The existing sensor test passes only an atom.

   **Smallest correction:** Remove event contents from this unsupported-operation error. Keep the trigger ID, runtime mode, and event type.

3. **P2 — Generated availability loses the required-policy flag.**  
   [projection_builder.ex:28](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect/jido/projection_builder.ex:28) copies policy names but omits `host_policy_required?`. Both projection structs also omit this field.

   Generated discovery passes these projections to `Authorization.connection_availability/4`. The missing flag defaults to `false`. Thus, a connected account with sufficient scopes can see `:available` when execution requires a host policy. This affects real declarations, including [Jira plan listing](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect_jira/lib/jido_connect/jira/actions/plans.ex:24). Execution still rejects the request through the complete specification.

   **Smallest correction:** Add the flag to action and sensor projections. Check that generated availability agrees with availability calculated from the specification.

4. **P2 — Adapter option lists discard supported runtime controls.**  
   [runtime_context.ex:81](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect/jido/runtime_context.ex:81) omits `provider_client`. [catalog/input.ex:6](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect/catalog/input.ex:6) omits both `provider_client` and `request_timeout_ms`.

   A host-supplied Jira client therefore reaches direct Connect calls but is lost through generated actions. Jira then selects its built-in client. Catalog calls also discard a host timeout that MCP-backed providers such as Trello use. I reproduced the catalog option loss. Existing provider tests demonstrate client injection through direct calls, but do not check adapter parity.

   **Smallest correction:** Forward these supported controls from trusted action context. Keep the common option list in one place and test the generated and catalog paths.

**Design improvements**

- **P2 — Put a complete v3 host example in the package guide.**  
  [README.md:310](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect/README.md:310) presents `plugin_spec/1` as installation, although it returns discovery data. [README.md:601](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect/README.md:601) says Jido schedules generated sensors, contrary to the current host contract.

  Also explain state assembly for the [suggested catalog routes](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect/catalog/plugin.ex:12). Their actions return only catalog results. Pinned Jido uses that output as the complete next Agent state, so direct routing can lose other state or fail validation. Show a host wrapper that preserves domain state, and test it through `Agent.cmd/3`. [Pinned Agent execution contract](https://github.com/agentjido/jido/blob/b02052402a6f1c4be10098c2d560831f14daec58/lib/jido/agent/command/runner.ex#L120-L132)

- **P3 — Define how a host supplies fresh poll context.**  
  [sensor_runtime.ex:13](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect/jido/sensor_runtime.ex:13) stores the initial context; each tick reuses it. Hosts must refresh short-lived leases, but the public callback guide gives no update operation. Document a supported context replacement step, or add a small helper that preserves the checkpoint. Scheduling and credential renewal should remain host responsibilities.

**Known upstream limits**

The catalog Plugin uses the correct pinned v3 `prepare/2` contract. Provider `.Plugin` modules are intentionally discovery modules. Generated sensors are intentionally process-free adapters. These distinctions are not defects. [Pinned Plugin contract](https://github.com/agentjido/jido/blob/b02052402a6f1c4be10098c2d560831f14daec58/lib/jido/plugin.ex#L52-L102)

The exact Git dependency for Jido remains the recorded publication constraint. I found no new upstream defect in this scope.

**Cleanup order:** Fix filter authority and error redaction first. Then restore metadata and option propagation. Finish the packaged host examples.

**Coverage:** Generated actions, projections, sensor callbacks, discovery filtering and availability, catalog Plugin, runtime context, and relevant callers/tests.

**Verification limits:** Local dependency folders and build files contain v2 versions. I downloaded the pinned v3 sources separately; Action and Signal archive checksums match the lockfile. I ran isolated option-merging and sanitizer checks. I did not run the full suite or validate the recorded quality results again.

Full independent review: Jido Connect v3 review: Catalog
Source task: 01a09c57-210c-79f0-9e9f-669bbeed6dfc

Reviewed `release/3.0` at `fb5b59bda429b7545f82072dabe10f8b299432dc`. The checkout is clean and unchanged. `bw prime` completed.

I found six confirmed defects.

1. **P1 — Reviewed packs ignore their filters.**  
   [catalog.ex:359](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect/lib/jido_connect/catalog.ex:359) applies only the allow-list. A pack with `filters: %{risk: :write}` and the read action `"catalog.item.get"` returns no normal items, but `reviewed_items/2` returns a fingerprinted read item. A pack with only `type: :action` also fails if its provider has triggers. Apply the same pack filters to the exact supplied modules before selection and fingerprint generation. Existing reviewed tests use matching filters and allow-lists, which conceal this defect.

2. **P2 — Pack restrictions change after JSON storage.**  
   [pack.ex:362](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect/lib/jido_connect/catalog/pack.ex:362) accepts all atom filter keys. The string-key path recognizes only some keys. Thus `%{status: :unavailable}` excludes an available provider, but the same pack returns that provider after JSON encoding and decoding. `category`, `visibility`, `package`, and other provider filters have the same problem. Use one supported-key list for atom and string keys. Reject unsupported keys with a validation error.

3. **P2 — Legacy describe and call functions reject valid `ToolEntry` references.**  
   [catalog.ex:230](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect/lib/jido_connect/catalog.ex:230) and [catalog.ex:263](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect/lib/jido_connect/catalog.ex:263) pass the reference directly to the Item API. A `ToolEntry` from `lookup_tool/2` succeeds in another lookup, but describe and call return `:invalid_tool_ref`. The previous implementation routed both functions through `lookup_tool/2`. Apply the existing `compatibility_item_ref/1` conversion in both adapters. The current tests check this reference form only for lookup.

4. **P2 — An unloaded ranker module cannot run.**  
   [ranker.ex:47](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect/lib/jido_connect/catalog/ranker.ex:47) checks `function_exported?/3` without loading the module. A valid ranker BEAM on the code path produces fallback results until another caller loads it. The probe returned the requested order immediately after `Code.ensure_loaded!/1`. Load the module before checking `rank/2`. Current test modules are already loaded when their tests run.

5. **P2 — Ranker input loses candidates and gains a string entry.**  
   [ranker.ex:33](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect/lib/jido_connect/catalog/ranker.ex:33) sends the complete candidate list through the bounded transport sanitizer. With 60 results, the ranker receives 50 candidate maps followed by `"[truncated 10 items]"`. It cannot rank the last ten items, and a callback that expects maps can fail. Sanitize each candidate without changing the outer list structure. If a candidate limit is needed, make it explicit and report it.

6. **P2 — Pack serialization fails for supported tuple references.**  
   [serializer.ex:82](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect/lib/jido_connect/catalog/serializer.ex:82) copies `allowed_tools` without normalization. A valid pack built with `[{:catalog, "catalog.item.get"}]` raises `Protocol.UndefinedError` when `Catalog.to_map/1` output is passed to Jason. Normalize references to stable strings before serialization. Converting tuples to JSON arrays alone would not preserve the accepted reference format.

Two design improvements would reduce maintenance cost.

- **P2 — Expose item projection errors through diagnostics.**  
  [catalog.ex:300](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect/lib/jido_connect/catalog.ex:300) reads each provider spec again after discovery. At line 315, it converts every item projection error to `[]`. Provider diagnostics cannot report these later failures. Preserve the error in an item diagnostic result. Reuse the first spec where practical. Keep the existing lenient list API.

- **P3 — Remove the unused second fingerprint projection.**  
  [reviewed_descriptor.ex:26](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect/lib/jido_connect/catalog/reviewed_descriptor.ex:26) still fingerprints `ToolDescriptor` directly. The public reviewed adapter now fingerprints `Item` and then converts it. Repository searches found no caller for the old `project/2` function. Remove that internal path and its metadata helper so there is one fingerprint definition. Keep the public legacy adapters.

The documented Jido Git dependency, Cowlib findings, and legacy MCP notification gap remain known upstream limitations. They are separate from these Catalog findings. I did not treat allowed v3 prereleases or the intentional MCP package removal as defects.

Fix pack selection and storage first, then the legacy adapters and ranker defects. Next, improve diagnostics and remove the unused fingerprint path.

Coverage included Item construction, discovery, filters, search, ranking, packs, fingerprints, serialization, describe/call paths, plugin inputs, legacy adapters, tests, and provider pack callers. Targeted probes confirmed the six defects. All eight existing reviewed-catalog tests passed in the temporary probe process.

I did not run a shared build or the full v3 suite. The shared dependency/build directories contain Action v2 artifacts; the probes recompiled current Catalog source and required contracts in a temporary process. No source, dependency, lockfile, branch, issue, package, or `jido_mcp` file was changed.

Full independent review: Jido Connect v3 review: Execution controls
Source task: 01a09c57-236c-7ba3-a07a-8bbe84647d97

I confirmed five defects. Fix the two P1 items before publication.

The checkout is clean. The branch is `release/3.0`, at the expected commit `fb5b59bda429b7545f82072dabe10f8b299432dc`.

1. **P1 — Commit can skip required confirmation after an actor change.**  
   [execution_authorization.ex:56](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect/lib/jido_connect/runtime/execution_authorization.ex:56) trusts the stored `confirmation_required?` flag. The [snapshot check](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect/lib/jido_connect/runtime/runtime.ex:383) does not bind the actor or check this flag again.  
   **Evidence:** Prepare a `:required_for_ai` action as a user. Commit it as an agent with the same connection, lease, and binding. The handler runs without approval. Changing a stored `:always` action’s confirmation flag to `false` also permits execution.  
   **Correction:** Bind the actor identity to the snapshot. Calculate confirmation requirements again from the current action and context. Reject an inconsistent stored flag.

2. **P1 — MCP wildcard scopes bypass lease scope limits.**  
   [scope_resolver.ex:85](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect/lib/jido_connect/mcp/scope_resolver.ex:85) removes a target requirement when the durable connection contains its wildcard. It does not check whether the lease still grants that wildcard.  
   **Evidence:** With endpoint and tool wildcards on the connection, authorization returned `:ok` when the effective lease contained only `mcp:tools:call`. The requested target had no effective lease grant. This contradicts the declared scope intersection contract. Resources and prompts use the same helper.  
   **Correction:** Check wildcard grants against effective lease scopes. Keep an explicit target or wildcard requirement in the authorization result.

3. **P2 — Approval callbacks can delay execution past expiry.**  
   [runtime.ex:109](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect/lib/jido_connect/runtime/runtime.ex:109) checks snapshot expiry before policy and approval callbacks. At [runtime.ex:126](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect/lib/jido_connect/runtime/runtime.ex:126), execution follows approval validation without another expiry check.  
   **Evidence:** A 300 ms validator delay let the handler run after both the snapshot and its 200 ms lease had expired.  
   **Correction:** Check snapshot and lease expiry again after callbacks, immediately before the handler call. Apply the lease check to invoke and poll paths too.

4. **P2 — The action hash omits authorization fields.**  
   [execution_snapshot.ex:20](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect/lib/jido_connect/runtime/execution_snapshot.ex:20) omits `host_policy_required?`, `policies`, and auth profile fields.  
   **Evidence:** Prepare with `host_policy_required?: true`. Change it to `false`, then commit without a policy callback. The hash remains equal and the handler runs. Approval thus remains valid after a change to the action’s authorization contract.  
   **Correction:** Add the authorization fields to the hash. Review the omitted schema fields at the same time.

5. **P2 — A valid approval module fails before its first load.**  
   [execution_authorization.ex:97](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect/lib/jido_connect/runtime/execution_authorization.ex:97) checks exported functions without first loading the module.  
   **Evidence:** An available but unloaded module with `validate/3` returned a configuration error. The same commit succeeded after `Code.ensure_loaded!/1`. Policy and scope callbacks already load their modules first.  
   **Correction:** Call `Code.ensure_loaded/1` before the export checks. Return a normalized error if loading fails.

Two smaller design improvements are useful:

- **P3 — Reject malformed successful scope results.** At [scope_requirements.ex:65](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect/lib/jido_connect/runtime/scope_requirements.ex:65), `{:ok, nil}` becomes an empty scope list. An isolated check reached the handler with no granted scopes. No current resolver returning this value was found. Require a list inside `{:ok, scopes}`.
- **P3 — State the credential revision requirement clearly.** The [lease hash](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect/lib/jido_connect/runtime/execution_snapshot.ex:45) includes public identity but excludes credential values. Document that a credential change must also change a bound public revision. Keep secrets outside the snapshot.

The host-owned approval store and atomic execution claim are correct package boundaries. Repeated commit calls are explicitly permitted by core’s storage-free design. I did not classify this as a defect.

Known upstream limits remain separate: the Jido Git dependency, Cowlib audit exceptions, and legacy MCP notification gap are recorded in [v3_status.md](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/docs/v3_status.md).

**Cleanup order:** Fix confirmation and MCP scope checks first. Then fix expiry, action hashes, and module loading. Add focused regression cases for each.

**Coverage:** Authorization, policy callbacks, lease binding and scopes, prepare/commit, stored snapshots, confirmation, expiry, and uncertain-write classification.

**Verification limits:** All 37 selected existing tests passed. Separate isolated checks reproduced the five defects. Relevant current source modules were loaded in a separate BEAM process because shared build files were older. No shared build, live provider call, full quality run, or package build was performed. Source, dependencies, lockfiles, and branch state remain unchanged.

Full independent review: Jido Connect v3 review: MCP client
Source task: 01a09c57-2619-7251-b3f3-113072d196ce

Reviewed `release/3.0` at `fb5b59bda429b7545f82072dabe10f8b299432dc`. The checkout is unchanged.

I found seven confirmed Connect defects.

1. **P1 — Connections can share a client across tenants.**  
   [endpoint_lease_manager.ex:246](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect/lib/jido_connect/mcp/endpoint_lease_manager.ex:246)

   Manager keys use `connection.id` without `tenant_id`. Two tenants with the same connection ID and ownership versions can reuse one generation. A live test with two BEAM servers confirmed that tenant B received tenant A’s tool result. Revocation also affects both tenants.

   **Correction:** Include tenant identity in record, generation, and ownership-barrier keys. Carry that identity through lifecycle APIs.

2. **P1 — Wildcard scopes bypass lease scope limits.**  
   [scope_resolver.ex:85](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect/lib/jido_connect/mcp/scope_resolver.ex:85)

   When the connection has a wildcard, the resolver removes the target scope requirement. Authorization then cannot detect that the lease excludes that wildcard. A lease containing only `mcp:tools:call` passed authorization for an arbitrary endpoint and tool. Resources, prompts, completion, and sessions use the same helper.

   **Correction:** Require the wildcard scope instead of returning an empty requirement. Check it against the effective lease scopes.

3. **P1 — Another lease can extend a session past its own expiry.**  
   [endpoint_lease_manager.ex:253](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect/lib/jido_connect/mcp/endpoint_lease_manager.ex:253)

   Acquisition extends the shared generation expiry. Tokens contain no individual expiry. A short lease’s token remained dispatchable after expiry when another acquisition supplied a longer lease. Session event delivery and its periodic checks use this shared state.

   **Correction:** Put the individual lease expiry in each token. Check both token expiry and generation state. Existing renewal tests check the renewed token, but not the expired original token.

4. **P2 — A slow handshake blocks unrelated lease controls.**  
   [endpoint_lease_manager.ex:274](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect/lib/jido_connect/mcp/endpoint_lease_manager.ex:274)

   Client startup runs inside the single manager process. An 800 ms handshake delayed revocation of another connection by 671 ms. With the default 30-second handshake, unrelated controls can exceed their five-second call timeout. Session lease checks use those controls.

   **Correction:** Start clients outside the manager callback. Before accepting the result, check the lease and ownership barrier again.

5. **P2 — Schema checks accept unhandled constraints.**  
   [schema_compatibility.ex:7](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect/lib/jido_connect/mcp/schema_compatibility.ex:7)

   The comparison ignores constraints such as `allOf`. Adding an `allOf` rule that removed an allowed action still returned `true`. A JSON Schema validator rejected that action. This path has real callers: Trello and X supply `required_schema` to typed calls.

   **Correction:** Reject unsupported validation keywords unless compatibility is established. Add the demonstrated `allOf` case to the tests.

6. **P2 — Static endpoints skip uncertain-write normalization.**  
   [runtime.ex:111](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect/lib/jido_connect/mcp/runtime.ex:111)

   The static endpoint path returns the client error directly. An unknown send result returned `reason: :outcome_unknown` and `mutation?: false`. The managed path returns the documented `:mcp_write_uncertain` and `mutation?: true`. Delivery remains `:sent_outcome_unknown`, but hosts receive inconsistent write classification.

   **Correction:** Use one write-result classifier for static and managed endpoints. The existing uncertain-write test covers only managed endpoints.

7. **P2 — Status ignores the declared timeout.**  
   [ex_mcp_client.ex:200](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect/lib/jido_connect/mcp/ex_mcp_client.ex:200)

   `status/2` discards its options. A test requested one millisecond and received success after 81 milliseconds. ExMCP’s status call uses its fixed GenServer timeout.

   **Correction:** Add timeout support to ExMCP’s public status API and pass the Connect timeout through it.

There is also **new upstream evidence**, separate from the known legacy notification limit:

- **P1 — ExMCP accepts a broader notification filter from the server.**  
  [ExMCP subscription.ex:157](/var/folders/8l/nyn2qp4d441b1zrgypxgry7m0000gn/T/connect-mcp-review-dmjzx4fq/ex_mcp_1_3_0/lib/ex_mcp/client/subscription.ex:157)

  The locked ExMCP package accepted an acknowledgment that added an unrequested private resource. On reconnect, it uses that acknowledged filter for automatic resource reads. Connect authorizes the requested filter, then forwards the resulting snapshot.

  **Correction:** ExMCP must reject acknowledgments that expand the requested filter before it starts automatic reads. Keep protocol handling in ExMCP. Connect must retain and enforce its authorized scope.

One **P3 design improvement** would reduce support work: document generation-wide schema binding. [endpoint_lease_manager.ex:355](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect/lib/jido_connect/mcp/endpoint_lease_manager.ex:355) intentionally keeps the first tool hash for a generation. Existing tests confirm this behavior. The guide should explain how to advance the generation after a reviewed schema change.

Fix tenant separation, lease scope checks, and individual expiry first. Resolve the upstream filter defect before relying on authorized reconnect reads. Then address startup blocking, schema checks, error classification, and status timeout.

Coverage included tools, resources, templates, prompts, completion, scopes, endpoints, leases, notifications, reconnect, pagination, schema checks, and the ExMCP adapter. I checked callers and relevant tests.

Nine isolated reproductions confirmed the reported paths. The downloaded ExMCP 1.3.0 archive matched the lockfile checksum. Local dependency caches were stale; other cached libraries supported the focused tests. I did not rerun full quality checks or claim a clean release build. The known legacy notification gap and Cowlib findings remain separate and unchanged.

Full independent review: Jido Connect v3 review: Provider helpers
Source task: 01a09c57-2858-7750-b28e-72cf480d2cec

Reviewed `release/3.0` at `fb5b59bda429b7545f82072dabe10f8b299432dc`. The checkout was clean and remained unchanged.

I confirmed six defects.

1. **P1 — Workflow polling can omit updates on later pages.**  
   [workflow_run_updates_poller.ex:41](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect_github/lib/jido_connect/github/handlers/triggers/workflow_run_updates_poller.ex:41)

   The poller always requests page 1. It then advances the checkpoint to the latest timestamp on that page. If another updated run is on page 2, that run is never read. The client returns `total_count`, but the poller ignores it. The `checkpoint` parameter also does not enter the HTTP query.

   An isolated check reproduced this omission. Existing tests cover successive ticks with one page. **Correction:** read all required pages before advancing the checkpoint. Keep the old checkpoint if any page fails.

2. **P2 — One error can give conflicting retry instructions.**  
   [error.ex:451](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect/lib/jido_connect/support/error.ex:451), [http.ex:114](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect/lib/jido_connect/provider/http.ex:114)

   `Http.provider_error/2` stores a public response map before the runtime adds action context. `Error.with_action_context/2` updates only the outer error.

   For a write without provider idempotency that times out, the resulting public error says `do_not_retry`, while `details.response.retry_guidance` says `safe_to_retry`. The isolated check confirmed both values in the same error. Existing action-context tests construct errors directly and miss this path.

   **Correction:** produce retry guidance after action context is complete, or update the nested response at the same time.

3. **P2 — Google and Microsoft code exchanges omit the PKCE verifier.**  
   [Google oauth.ex:48](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect_google/lib/jido_connect/google/oauth.ex:48), [Microsoft oauth.ex:48](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect_microsoft/lib/jido_connect/microsoft/oauth.ex:48)

   Both authorization helpers accept `code_challenge` and `code_challenge_method`. Neither token exchange includes `code_verifier`, even when the caller supplies it. Captured request bodies confirmed the omission for both providers.

   A PKCE exchange requires this verifier. [RFC 7636, section 4.5](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7636.txt) Existing exchange tests do not check this field. **Correction:** include the optional verifier in the exchange form and test the outgoing request. The host must continue to own verifier storage.

4. **P2 — OAuth URL composition corrupts existing query parameters.**  
   [oauth.ex:22](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect/lib/jido_connect/provider/oauth.ex:22)

   The helper always adds `"?"`. With endpoint `https://provider.test/auth?tenant=one`, it produces:

   ```text
   https://provider.test/auth?tenant=one?client_id=client&state=state
   ```

   Parsing this URL puts `?client_id=client` inside the tenant value. The `client_id` parameter is absent. Google and Microsoft expose endpoint overrides, so callers can reach this case.

   **Correction:** filter blank values, then use the existing `Http.url_with_query/2`. Add a test with an existing query.

5. **P2 — Google and Microsoft error normalization removes retry metadata.**  
   [Google transport.ex:39](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect_google/lib/jido_connect/google/transport.ex:39), [Microsoft transport.ex:69](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect_microsoft/lib/jido_connect/microsoft/transport.ex:69)

   Map error responses bypass the shared response conversion. A `429` response with `Retry-After: 30` loses that interval when converted to a provider error. These clauses also ignore supplied mutation and idempotency options.

   Google Sheets and Graph action callers use this path. Microsoft tests check header extraction separately from error normalization; they do not verify that callers receive the metadata.

   **Correction:** preserve the common response fields from the original response, then add the provider-specific message. Pass the operation options through.

6. **P2 — Valid JSON with an invalid webhook shape can raise an exception.**  
   [webhook.ex:53](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect/lib/jido_connect/provider/webhook.ex:53), [Slack verification.ex:57](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect_slack/lib/jido_connect/slack/webhook/verification.ex:57)

   The shared decoder declares a map-or-list result but accepts scalars. A correctly signed body containing `42` passes decoding and raises `FunctionClauseError` in Slack delivery verification. Existing tests cover invalid JSON syntax, not invalid decoded shapes.

   **Correction:** enforce the declared shared result types. Require a map at the Slack boundary and return a normalized `:invalid_payload` error.

Two design improvements are separate from these defects:

- **P3 — Make connection ID defaults suitable for multiple accounts.** [Google connections.ex:30](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect_google/lib/jido_connect/google/connections.ex:30) and [Microsoft connections.ex:31](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect_microsoft/lib/jido_connect/microsoft/connections.ex:31) derive user connection IDs only from `owner_id`. Two provider accounts for one application user receive the same default ID. Explicit host IDs already solve this. Require or clearly document them for multiple-account use; add a two-account example.

- **P3 — Define the scope of the runtime timeout option.** [runtime.ex:55](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect/lib/jido_connect/runtime/runtime.ex:55) validates and forwards `request_timeout_ms`, but the reviewed REST helpers do not consume it. X and Trello adapters do. Document this limit or pass the option through the REST clients. Do not imply a common deadline until it is enforced.

The Cowlib audit exceptions and legacy MCP notification gap remain recorded upstream limitations in [v3_status.md](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/docs/v3_status.md). They are separate from these findings.

Cleanup order: fix polling loss, unify retry information, repair OAuth, then validate webhook shapes. Keep provider-specific corrections in their provider packages.

Coverage included shared HTTP, OAuth, webhook, polling, response and error helpers; representative GitHub, Slack, Google, Microsoft, Jira, and Nextcloud callers; and related tests.

Seven isolated checks confirmed the defect behavior using current source and existing dependency builds. I did not rerun umbrella builds, live provider tests, or dependency audits. The recorded full-suite results were reviewed but not independently repeated.

Full independent review: Jido Connect v3 review: Runtime results
Source task: 01a09c57-2ac2-7981-8f33-21ede2d89ca2

Reviewed `release/3.0` at `fb5b59bda429b7545f82072dabe10f8b299432dc`. The checkout is clean and unchanged. I found seven confirmed defects.

1. **P1 — Callback failures can expose credentials.**  
   [callback.ex:48](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect/lib/jido_connect/support/callback.ex:48) stores exception messages and formatted stack traces in public error details. A handler that calls `Map.fetch!(credentials, :missing_key)` exposes the credential map through `Error.to_map/1`. A function-clause failure also exposes credentials through stack-trace arguments. Both cases were reproduced. [telemetry.ex:78](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect/lib/jido_connect/support/telemetry.ex:78) uses the same unsafe text conversion.  
   **Correction:** Keep the exception type and stack frames without argument values. Use a fixed public message. Key redaction cannot remove credentials after conversion to text.

2. **P1 — Tuples and keyword lists bypass key redaction.**  
   [sanitizer.ex:162](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect/lib/jido_connect/support/sanitizer.ex:162) treats keyword lists as ordinary lists. The telemetry tuple clause at line 180 calls `inspect/2` without recursive redaction. Thus `[access_token: "secret"]` retains the value in both profiles. A map with an access token inside a transport-error tuple also survives `Http.provider_error/2` and `Error.to_map/1`. These cases were reproduced. Existing tests cover map redaction and simple tuple conversion.  
   **Correction:** Recognize key/value lists and redact sensitive values. Recursively sanitize tuple contents before formatting.

3. **P1 — Public provider responses expose raw error reasons.**  
   [provider_response.ex:115](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect/lib/jido_connect/contracts/provider_response.ex:115) copies `response.reason` without sanitization. The field accepts any term, including a Req error reason such as `{:invalid_header_value, "authorization", value}`. The public map and custom `Inspect` expose that value. The tuple also makes JSON encoding fail. Both effects were reproduced.  
   **Correction:** Normalize transport reasons to stable codes. Put only sanitized diagnostic data in a separate field. Apply the same rules to the public map and `Inspect`.

4. **P2 — The HTTP error helper retains response bodies under `message`.**  
   [http.ex:135](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect/lib/jido_connect/provider/http.ex:135) returns the complete body map when it has no `"message"` field. The helper stores that map in `details.message`. Body summarization removes `details.body`, but leaves this copy. A response with `%{"content" => "private-body-marker"}` retained the content in the public error. Multiple provider transports use this helper.  
   **Correction:** Use a fixed fallback message. Accept an explicit message only when it has the expected scalar type. Keep other response content in the body summary.

5. **P2 — One failure can give conflicting retry instructions.**  
   [error.ex:451](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect/lib/jido_connect/support/error.ex:451) adds action risk and mutation context only to the outer error. The nested response from `Http.provider_error/2` retains its earlier retry decision. For a non-idempotent write timeout, the reproduced public error said `:do_not_retry`, while `details.response.retry_guidance` said `"safe_to_retry"`. A host UI or retry worker can receive opposite instructions from the same result.  
   **Correction:** Calculate retry guidance once after action context is known. Remove the duplicate nested decision or update it from that final context.

6. **P2 — Binary truncation can produce invalid JSON text.**  
   [sanitizer.ex:214](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect/lib/jido_connect/support/sanitizer.ex:214) cuts binaries at an arbitrary byte boundary. With 511 ASCII bytes followed by `é`, the default 512-byte limit splits the UTF-8 character. `String.valid?/1` returned false and `Jason.encode/1` failed. This affects otherwise valid provider messages and webhook payloads. Existing truncation tests use ASCII text.  
   **Correction:** Cut valid text at a UTF-8 boundary. Define a safe representation for input binaries that are already invalid UTF-8.

7. **P2 — Invalid poll envelopes escape as raw exceptions.**  
   [runtime.ex:162](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect/lib/jido_connect/runtime/runtime.ex:162) calls `Map.get/3` before checking the poll result type. A handler returning `{:ok, nil}` caused `Connect.poll/4` to raise `BadMapError`, outside the callback normalization boundary. Existing tests cover invalid `signals` inside a map, but not an invalid envelope.  
   **Correction:** Validate the result map before reading it. Return a normalized `ExecutionError` for an invalid envelope.

One **P3 design improvement** concerns audit records. [event.ex:2](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect/lib/jido_connect/contracts/event.ex:2) describes a “redacted” record, but its constructors retain payload and metadata values unchanged. `Run` also has no public serialization helper. I found contract tests, but no core runtime creation path for these records. Host ownership makes that absence valid. Clarify that hosts must sanitize these records, or provide an explicit safe-map helper. Do not add persistence to core.

The local status record lists remaining Cowlib audit exceptions and the ExMCP legacy-notification gap. These are known upstream limitations, separate from the defects above. I did not recheck upstream status.

Fix credential exposure first, then body retention and retry consistency, then UTF-8 handling and poll validation. Clarify audit-record documentation last.

Coverage included shared HTTP results, error normalization, sanitizer profiles, telemetry, action and poll results, generated adapters, MCP result paths, and audit contracts. **All 23 selected existing tests passed.** Isolated checks reproduced all seven defects using current source loaded into memory and existing dependency builds. The [reproduction script](/tmp/jido-runtime-review.dM0acC/repro.exs) uses fake credentials. I did not run a shared build, the full suite, live provider calls, a fresh dependency audit, or a package build.

title: Refine Jido Connect v3 from nine independent code reviews
